question.worked_solution:
If we let $u=2+3\operatorname{tan}⁡(x),$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{sec}^{2}⁡(x)\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={sec}^{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\pi /4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $5$ |

Using the above, we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡(x)}{2+3\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{2+3\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)}\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|{|}_{2}^{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{5}{2})\end{aligned}
$$
